requirements.original: The rotate left (<@) operator accepts two operands.
requirements.canonical: The rotate left operator `<@` IS a binary operator taking a left-hand and a right-hand operand.

requirements.original: It rotates the left-hand operand by the number of shift units to the left as specified by the right-hand operand.
requirements.canonical: The rotate left operator `<@` rotates the left-hand operand to the left by the number of rotate units specified by the right-hand operand.

ambiguity.issue: 'shift units' is used in the rotate clause, while the list above defines 'rotate unit'.

requirements.header: // @requirement: 7.1.7 -- It rotates the left-hand operand by the number of shift units to the left as specified by the right-hand operand.

requirements.original: Excess shift units (bits, hexadecimal digits, octets, characters, or elements) are re-inserted into the left-hand operand from its right-hand side.
requirements.canonical: For the rotate left operator `<@`, the rotate units shifted out on the left IS re-inserted into the left-hand operand from its right-hand side.

ambiguity.issue: 'Excess shift units' is used where 'rotate units' (as defined in the list) is meant.

requirements.header: // @requirement: 7.1.7 -- Excess shift units (bits, hexadecimal digits, octets, characters, or elements) are re-inserted into the left-hand operand from its right-hand side.

requirements.condition: the left-hand operand is of a record of, set of or array type
requirements.header: // @requirement: 7.1.7 -- a) When the rotate operator is used for record of-s, set of-s and arrays, its left hand operand shall be at least partially initialized.

requirements.original: NOTE 2: Note that for the right hand operand restriction a) in clause 6.5 further on applies.

The right-hand operand of a rotate operator SHALL satisfy the general operator restriction a) of clause 7.1 (operands shall be initialized/of compatible type), the reference to 6.5 being outdated.

requirements.original: This operator is allowed for data objects of all data types that are a union-field-reference or a type alternative of an anytype.
requirements.canonical: The operand of the `ischosen` operator SHALL be a reference to an alternative of a union type or to a type alternative of an `anytype`.

ambiguity.issue: 'is allowed for data objects of all data types that are a union-field-reference' is garbled: it is unclear whether other operands are forbidden (compile-time error) or merely meaningless; it also conflicts with 7.1.8.0 ('operand can be of any type'). Chosen reading: exclusive restriction.
readings: The operand of `ischosen` SHALL be a reference to a union alternative or anytype alternative; any other operand is an error.
The operand of `ischosen` MAY be a reference to a union alternative or anytype alternative, other operands being allowed as for all presence checking operators.

requirements.original: The ischosen operator is applicable to data objects of union types or of anytype containing a specific value or a value list.
requirements.canonical: The `ischosen` operator IS applicable to data objects of union types or `anytype` that contain a specific value or a value list.

ambiguity.issue: It is unclear whether applying `ischosen` to a union template containing another matching mechanism (e.g. `?`) is an error or yields false; EXAMPLE 1 (mw_u3 := ?) shows false. Chosen reading: other templates yield false.
readings: `ischosen` applied to a union/anytype template that is neither a specific value nor a value list yields `false`.
`ischosen` SHALL NOT be applied to a union/anytype template that is neither a specific value nor a value list (error).

requirements.canonical: If the operand of `ischosen` is a value list, the operator returns `true` if all members of the value list have the referenced alternative selected.
requirements.condition: the operand is a value list

requirements.header: // @requirement: 7.1.8.2 -- The result is false if there is another alternative of the union type or anytype on which ischosen would return true.
